inspection_summary: Inspected all 1121 frozen splitter-defined lines of the article. The source develops a transition-range refinement of zero pair correlation under RH and a quantitative twin-prime hypothesis, routes singular-series error through an integrated remainder f, builds a compact smooth cutoff with explicit Fourier decay, reduces F(x,T) to two Dirichlet-polynomial mean values, and recombines three correction integrals to obtain the theorem, its two asymptotic corollaries, and a three-regime conjecture. The displayed mathematics is mostly recoverable from prose and neighboring formulas; lines 838-840 are not independently recoverable and several formula-heavy spans retain text-layer risk.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Transition-scale matching from two endpoint laws
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source treats the neighborhood of x=T as a matching problem: retain lower-order corrections in a broad conditional formula, then show distinct collections become negligible on opposite sides to recover compatible endpoint asymptotics.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is conditional on RH and the stated quantitative twin-prime conjecture, and the final three-regime statement remains conjectural.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Arithmetic discrepancy compressed into one transferable remainder
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Centering singular-series sums and integrating their discrepancy into f turns several discrete arithmetic errors into a common analytic object whose appearances in head and tail transforms can be bounded or canceled.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The quantitative quality of f inherits the strong prime-pair hypothesis and exact coefficients remain formula-layout-sensitive.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Smoothing as a removable proof interface
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Iterated averaging constructs a cutoff strong enough to import mean-value estimates, while explicit Fourier control later replaces that auxiliary cutoff by sine kernels with errors below the target scale.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source verifies this for its chosen cutoff and parameter regime; it does not establish a cutoff-independent theorem.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Three-component decomposition isolates discrete, head, and tail corrections
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The proof gains tractability by separating a discrete cosine-weighted singular-series term from two complementary centered-error transforms, evaluating each in its natural representation, and recombining only after cancellations are explicit.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a source-specific proof architecture, not evidence that the same decomposition is canonical for other zero-statistics problems.
